title: micro-instruction-routing-lattice-notes
content:
Working scratchpad for a compact "micro-instruction routing lattice" idea — quick brain dump before pairing with Arjun. Intention: enable fine-grained routing decisions inside a single inference request by annotating 'micro-instructions' (instruction fragments) with routing hints, cost budgets and fallbacks. Goal is not to replace per-request routing but to let a single call fan-out across specialized flows for parts of the prompt (e.g., tool calls, embeddings, hallucination-check fragments, terse facts).

High-level motivation
- Many complex requests contain semantically separable pieces: extraction, lookup, classification, synthesis. Routing them to targeted runtimes (cheap quantized vs. high-precision fp16) reduces cost and improves tail-latency.
- Current model-routing is coarse (per-request). We need an incremental, low-overhead mechanism that lives in the ingress path and composes responses.
- Keep developer ergonomics: a single API call should express micro-instructions via a small DSL or annotated JSON payload.

Rough API surface (sketch)
POST /v1/micro-route
payload:
{
  "request_id": "str — client generated",
  "input": "raw prompt string or list of segments",
  "micro_instructions": [
    {
      "id": "seg-1",
      "type": "extraction | lookup | embed | verify | synth",
      "span": {"start": 0, "end": 48},
      "hints": ["fast","use-cache"],
      "budget": {"cpu_ms": 10, "token_budget": 40},
      "fallback": "compatible-model:v2"
    }
  ],
  "global_policy": {"latency_slo_ms": 250, "cost_sensitivity": "high"}
}

Response:
{
  "request_id": "...",
  "parts": [
    {"id": "seg-1","status":"ok","result":"...","meta":{"latency_ms":32,"route":"dedicated-quantized-1"}},
    {"id": "final","status":"assembled","result":"full text"}
  ],
  "trace_id": "..."
}

Design notes / invariants
- Micro-instruction ids must be stable within one request so we can map telemetry and fallbacks.
- Routing decisions must be cheap (policy table lookup + scoring). No heavy model selection logic on hot path.
- Prefix/caching: allow micro-instructions to specify cache keys (deterministic inputs) to hit KV cache without invoking runtime.
- Assembly: lightweight combiner runs last and may include simple stitching rules (whitespace, punctuation hints). For complex merges, return flagged and let client reconcile.
- Telemetry: per-part latency, token_count, cost_estimate. Store aggregated per-request and per-micro-type metrics.

Routing lattice concept (text diagram)

  [Ingress] -> parse -> annotate -> policy-scoring -> parallel routes -> combiner -> [response]
                          |                 |\
                          |                 | \-> fallback-tier
                          v                 v
                   policy-table (rules)   runtime-pool (fp16, int8, embedding-only)

Policy scoring: score = w_latency*predict_latency + w_cost*estimate_cost + w_quality*historical_quality
- weights pulled from global_policy or tenant defaults
- we keep small learnable heuristics, but default to rule-based mappings to avoid regressions

Config sketch (YAML-like)
routing_lattice:
  micro_types:
    extraction:
      preferred_runtime: "int8-fast"
      fallbacks: ["fp16-accurate"]
      qos: "mid"
    embed:
      preferred_runtime: "embedding-only"
      cacheable: true
  policy_table:
    - when: "micro.type == 'lookup' and input_length < 200"
      route: "dedicated-quantized"
      max_latency_ms: 120
    - when: "micro.hints contains 'verify'"
      route: "fp16-accurate"

Questions / open decisions
- How to represent dependencies between micro-instructions? (simple DAG vs. linear span order)
  - Option A: explicit depends_on array per micro. Simpler. But risk of deadlocks.
  - Option B: order-by-span and only allow forward dependencies.
- Failure semantics: if one micro fails, should we return partial assembled response or bubble error? likely configurable per-micro (continue_on_error true/false).
- Security: micro instructions could leak internal routing choices that reveal model types — sanitize in public responses.
- Backpressure: if too many micro fragments arrive, need admission control. Consider token-budget throttles per-request.

Experiment plan (short)
- Phase 0: simulator that takes recorded production traces and rewrites them into micro-instruction payloads. Measure idealized latency and cost improvements.
- Phase 1: internal feature flag run on 5% of traffic for low-risk micro types (embed, lookup). Compare tail latency, cost per logical request, error rate.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (overall + per-micro), cost-per-request ($ estimate), assembly-failure-rate, cache-hit-rate, fallback-rate.

Small checklist
- [ ] prototype ingress parser to accept annotated JSON
- [ ] implement policy-table interpreter (rules + weights)
- [ ] add per-micro telemetry schema to tracing system
- [ ] simulation job (replay historical calls) + cost model
- [ ] review security/privacy with compliance

Notes to self
- Keep API minimal initially: only 'type', 'span', 'hints', 'budget', 'fallback'. Avoid full DSL.
- Don't ship adaptive ML-based routing until we have strong guardrails and eval set.
- Coordinate with console team for dashboard surfaces: per-micro breakdown would be a great win for observability.

Random ideas to drop later
- micro-instruction prewarm: if a micro type appears frequently in a tenant, keep a warmed worker pinned for N requests.
- micro-affinity: prioritize same-host routing for span groups that were previously processed in same session to exploit warm KV caches.

End of initial sketch. Will expand after pairing session with Arjun (blocking: need quick simulator data).
